description: Synthetic-data study of BKT initial mastery priors P(L0) for the Sanskrit AI Tutor. Read-only with respect to production: no production constant, schema, endpoint or UI is modified by this experiment.

population.lesson_sampling: distinct lessons drawn from the full 25-lesson catalog, own-tier lessons upweighted by own_tier_sampling_weight

candidate_grid.note: Every production INITIAL_MASTERY value is an exact multiple of 0.01, so the grid already contains them; the flag is asserted at runtime rather than assumed.

mastery_threshold.note: A single consistent 0.7 threshold. Two different attempts-conditions apply to it (see REPORT.md section 8).

dgp.comment: HIDDEN DATA-GENERATING PARAMETERS. These are experimental assumptions, NOT measured properties of Sanskrit learners.

mean_modes.production: mu[group][tier] = production INITIAL_MASTERY[group][tier] exactly (assumes production seeds are unbiased population means)
mean_modes.group_mean_only: mu[group][tier] = mean over tiers of INITIAL_MASTERY[group] (removes the tier effect)
mean_modes.group_overlap: mu[group][tier] = mean over groups of INITIAL_MASTERY[group][tier] (removes the group effect, keeps tiers)

dgp.distribution: Beta, method-of-moments from (mu, within_group_sd), clipped to [0.001, 0.999]
dgp.observation_model: p(correct) = theta*(1-s) + (1-theta)*g ; y ~ Bernoulli(p) ; theta <- theta + (1-theta)*t after the attempt

scenarios.label: Primary: DGP aligned with production, production t/g/s
No tier effect in true mastery
True mastery 0.10 higher than production seeds
True mastery 0.10 lower than production seeds
Fewer lessons and questions per learner
Primary with a different random seed
Primary with a third random seed

strategies.production: one production INITIAL_MASTERY value per (group, tier)
strategies.common: a single prior shared by every group and every tier
strategies.group_x_tier: one prior per (group, tier) - structural match to production, reported as an extra comparison
strategies.oracle_reference: the hidden data-generating mean; simulation-only reference, unavailable in a real deployment
